definition_en: flattering or coaxing talk used to persuade
core_image: 一串抹了蜜的恭维话从嘴边流出来
scene: 旧货摊前，摊主的夸赞一句接一句。No amount of cajolery could lower the old collector's price.
sceneCN: 这里 cajolery 是「哄骗、甜言蜜语」（第 1 个义项：以恭维劝诱的言语）；句意是任凭摊主百般恭维，老藏家仍不降价。

pos.zh: 哄诱；甜言蜜语；奉承劝诱之词

derivatives.zh: 同根动词，义为「哄骗；甜言劝诱」
由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「哄劝地」
同根名词，义为「哄诱（行为）」

senses.title: Flattering persuasion
senses.definition: speech that flatters or coaxes in order to win someone over
senses.definitionCN: 以奉承或哄劝赢取他人的言语
senses.example: The salesman's cajolery softened the old customer.
senses.exampleCN: 推销员的甜言蜜语打动了老主顾。
senses.why: The -ery ending names the practice of the verb cajole.
senses.whyCN: -ery 词尾把动词 cajole 的行为总其名。

senses.title: Tactics of gentle deceit
senses.definition: the strategy or art of getting one's way through soft words
senses.definitionCN: 以软语达到目的的手段或心术
senses.example: Threats failed, so he turned to cajolery.
senses.exampleCN: 威吓无效，他便改用哄骗。
senses.why: What began as talk becomes a recognised tactic.
senses.whyCN: 言语之术一旦惯用，便成一种策略。

intro.en: Cajolery is cajole plus the noun suffix -ery, built on the French jay-cage word.
intro.cn: cajolery 由 cajole 加名词后缀 -ery 构成，根在法语的「松鸦与笼」。

items.en: behind Latin gaius, a jay, stands a reconstructed root for brightness or colour, uncertain in detail.
items.cn: 拉丁语 gaius（松鸦）背后是表「鲜亮、色彩」的重构词根，细节不确定。
拉丁语 gaius 指聒噪的松鸦。

items.en: cajoler meant to chatter coaxingly, from cage and jay words.
items.cn: 法语 cajoler 由「笼」与「松鸦」诸词演变，指甜言哄劝。

items.en: English borrowed cajole, then formed cajolery with -ery.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语借入 cajole，再以 -ery 构成 cajolery。

items.en: cajolery now belongs to the rhetoric of persuasion, often with a sly tone.
items.cn: 如今 cajolery 属劝说修辞，常带几分狡黠。

note.en: The look-alike group is the cajole family; the near-meaning group gathers flattery words.
note.cn: 形近组为 cajole 同族；近义组是奉承类词。

entries.definitionCN: 芹菜，仅拼写相近，词源无关

normalIntro.en: Cajolery is cajole with a warehouse of sweet talk attached.
normalIntro.cn: cajolery 就是 cajole 加上一座「甜话仓库」。

normal.en: The -ery suffix names a practice, as in trickery.
normal.cn: -ery 词尾指某种行径，如 trickery。

normal.en: Cajolery is the noun; cajole is the verb.
normal.cn: cajolery 是名词，cajole 是动词。

normal.en: Immune to cajolery means flattery does not work.
normal.cn: immune to cajolery 指不为甜言所动。

normal.en: Threats and cajolery are opposite tactics.
normal.cn: 威吓与哄骗是相反的手段。

abstract.en: Hear a syrup voice pour on the praise.
abstract.cn: 听糖浆般的嗓音把恭维一勺勺浇下来。

abstract.en: See the old man shake his head, unmoved.
Feel a gift being pressed into your hands.
abstract.cn: 感受有人硬把礼物塞进你手里。

examples.en: All her cajolery could not reopen the sealed door.
examples.cn: 她说尽好话，那扇封死的门仍未打开。

examples.en: The courtier mixed gifts with cajolery.
Bribery and cajolery were the regime's twin tools.
examples.cn: 贿赂与哄骗是这个政权的双刃。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卡·粥·哩」——哄劝到极致：粥都端到嘴边了，好话一路说到「哩」。

root: cajolery = cajole（法语「如笼中松鸦般甜言聒噪」）加 -ery（表行径的名词后缀）；其根是拉丁语松鸦 gaius；同族词 cajole、cajolement、cajolingly 同出一源。

sensesIntro.en: The verb's chatter is gathered into a noun: the whole stock of sweet talk, and the trick of using it.
sensesIntro.cn: 动词的聒噪被收进名词：整库甜言蜜语，及其使用的心术。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: syrup-toned praise poured on a stubborn listener.
core.cn: 核心意象：糖浆般的恭维浇向固执的听者。

branches.cn: 推销员没完没了的恭维

branches.en: the words and the art of using them

intro.en: The -ery suffix turns verbs into named practices, from trickery to cajolery.
intro.cn: -ery 词尾把动词变成「行径」之名，从 trickery 到 cajolery。

latinIntro.en: The deep root is the Latin jay gaius, reshaped in French.
latinIntro.cn: 深层词根是拉丁语松鸦 gaius，在法语中变形。
